newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia's SKB bid-only as trade resumes.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia's SKB bid-only as trade resumes.

text.p: Shares in Slovenian bank SKB were quoted at a buying indication only on Tuesday after trading was reinstated on the Ljubljana bourse following a one-week suspension.
In early trade, the bank was bid at 55,000 tolars, up more than 11 percent from its close on January 20 at 49,300 tolars.
Traders said SKB could well surge over 30 percent if the bourse decides to lift its daily 10 percent price swing limit amid no sellers.
"Nobody will sell SKB at 55,000. If the bourse lifts the limit the price could well go up to 70,000 or 75,000," Danilo Grasic, head of the investment sector at Creditanstalt said.
The bourse said it would consider abolishing the daily limit if there was no strike price in the first 30 minutes.
Demand for SKB has burgeoned due to the bank's plan to list global depository receipts on the London stock exchange by mid-February -- approved by the Bank of Slovenia last week.
SKB shares were suspended from Tuesday last week as by the day before their average price had risen over 30 percent since the bank's last public announcement on the price of its shares.

Bourse regulations stipulate that that trading be suspended after such a rise or fall until the company concerned issues a statement on why it thinks its share price has made such a move. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
